title: Protocol for real-time imaging of membrane fission by mitofissin
protocol: Prepare excess membrane reservoirs.
Add 40 μL of 5.0 M NaCl to 160 μL of liposome solution containing 250 μM of lipids.
Agitate the mixture intermittently with a vortex mixer for 30 min at 20°C–25°C.
Add 20 μL of suspension containing silica beads in water to the liposome solution.
Add 780 μL of water to the mixture and centrifuge it at 500 × g for 1 min at 25°C.
Remove ∼950 μL of the supernatant, being careful not to aspirate the beads pellet.
Add ∼950 μL of water to the beads pellet and centrifuge it at 500 × g for 1 min at 25°C.
Repeat steps removing liposomes remaining in the bulk solution three times.
Prepare an observation chamber assembled with a C-shaped silicone rubber spacer sandwiched between a cover glass and a glass slide.
Fill HEPES buffer containing 1 mg/mL of BSA into the observation chamber at 20°C–25°C.
Aspirate solution containing excess membrane reservoirs and deposit it at the open side of the observation chamber.
Tilt the observation chamber more than ∼20° for the excess membrane reservoirs to roll slowly toward the inside over the bottom.
Roll the excess membrane reservoirs until they reach the inside wall.
Place the observation chamber horizontally.
Put the observation chamber on the stage of confocal laser scanning microscope to observe lipid nanotubes.
Prepare a glass micropipette with a diameter of ∼20 μm using a puller and a capillary cleaving tool.
Load 100 μM of SpAtg44 in HEPES buffer into the micropipette by aspiration using a dry vacuum pump.
Connect the micropipette to a hydraulic system through a silicone tube.
Set the micropipette on the three-dimensional manipulator.
Adjust the voltage induced by application pressure to be ∼3 V (positive) in a digital multimeter.
Adjust the micropipette so that the tip is visible under the confocal laser scanning microscope.
Read and adjust the voltage induced by the application pressure using a digital multimeter to neutral value.
Position the tip of the micropipette near lipid nanotubes carefully.
Apply additional positive pressure up to 300 mV from the neutral voltage value to introduce SpAtg44.
Record time-lapse imaging during SpAtg44 application to lipid nanotubes using FV31S-SW software.
Take images of fluorescence from Liss Rhod PE excited by a 561 nm laser every ∼1-s for 15 min with ×60 oil immersion objective lens.
Analyze the time-lapse images using FV31S-SW or Fiji software to estimate fission events per tube length (40 μm).
Manually count fission sites along the nanotubes based on fluorescence breaks after subtracting background.
Estimate the radius of the lipid nanotube.
Assemble an observation chamber with a C-shaped silicone rubber spacer between a cover glass and a glass slide.
Fill the observation chamber with HEPES buffer lacking BSA.
Deposit 20 μL of the solution containing excess membrane reservoirs into the observation chamber.
Place the observation chamber on the stage of the confocal laser scanning microscope.
Take images of supported lipid bilayers spilled out from excess membrane reservoirs.
Measure the total fluorescence intensity and the membrane area in ROI after subtracting the background by Fiji software.
Plot the total fluorescence intensity against the membrane area to determine the α value by Excel software.
Measure the total fluorescence intensity and the length of the lipid nanotube in ROI after subtracting the background by Fiji software.
Estimate the tube radius, r, from the equation: r = I / 2πLα.
Plot the fission events per tube length against tube radius to visualize the tube radius dependency of fission activity.
